transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

I’m here because I spend most of the day checking things around the house—outlets, locks, tools, even dust—and fixing or rechecking them over and over. I get worn out, but I still don’t feel sure enough to just leave it alone.
What specific thought or fear goes through your mind if you try to stop yourself from checking?

Even if I know I did it right, I get these thoughts that I missed a loose wire and the house is going to burn down, or that I left a nail somewhere and my wife will get hurt. I try to tell myself it’s done, but the thoughts just come back stronger.
How long have you been dealing with these thoughts and repetitive checking behaviors?
I’m not really sure how long exactly. It’s been going on for a while, but I can’t pin down when it started.
How has this checking routine affected your ability to manage your daily responsibilities?

It’s affected things a lot. I stopped taking paid carpentry jobs because I can’t get out of the house without getting stuck checking everything. I’ve also pulled back from the community projects I used to help with. My wife does more of the errands and makes more of the decisions now, because I get caught up in it and end up exhausted.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of compulsive checking behaviors, repetitive fixing, and pathological doubt suggests obsessive-compulsive disorder, with generalized anxiety disorder and anankastic personality disorder as differential possibilities.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with classic obsessions (recurrent, intrusive thoughts that a loose wire will burn the house down or a stray nail will harm his wife) and compulsions (repetitive, time-consuming checking and fixing of outlets, locks, and tools). The patient attempts to resist these thoughts, but they persist and cause significant exhaustion and functional impairment, leading to cessation of paid carpentry work and social withdrawal.

confirmed_symptoms: Intrusive, distressing thoughts of catastrophic harm (house burning down, wife getting injured)
Thoughts return persistently despite attempts to dismiss or reassure oneself
Repetitive, ritualistic checking and rechecking of outlets, locks, tools, and dust
Spending most of the day checking to the point of exhaustion

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Present for an extended period ('going on for a while'), though exact onset date was not specified
additional_requirements: Obsessions and compulsions are recognized as originating from the patient's own mind
Compulsive acts are not experienced as inherently pleasurable and are performed to prevent feared harm
